Apply each capability finding to that agent's charter as a durable upgrade under a dated '## Charter upgrades' heading. An agent that repeats a known gap is a process defect.
outcome: Shared working agreement 10: the positive twin of the lessons ledger, so each iteration starts stronger. Produced the dated upgrade logs in both charters.

instruction: At hand-off, write one ledger line, then your own row file in a per-requirement, per-role rows folder. Never write a shared dashboard file another agent also writes; the requirements owner composes it.
outcome: Per CLAUDE.md earned method 6, a shared dashboard file blocked both merge trains at the merge door after each had gated cleanly.

instruction: Analyst closing-out (superseded): as your last action, set your row on the shared team dashboard to 'COMPLETE, AWAITING ASSIGNMENT' with a one-line verdict and artifact path, and append to the completion log.
outcome: The goal was stopping idle seats. Agents writing one shared file deadlocked both merge trains, and the card now routes hand-off rows to per-agent pod-rows files (business-system-analyst.card.md:30). The full charter still carries the old text.

instruction: Keep any list that changes (e.g. the merge gates) in ONE canonical place, and point to it everywhere else.
outcome: The gate list grew from five to eight inside two sessions, so a second copy is stale the day it is written.

instruction: Put the 'Lessons:' line IN THE ARTIFACT as its last line (format 'Lessons: L-3: clause, L-8: clause', or 'Lessons: none'), not only in the reply.
outcome: Two analysts in one session put a correct Lessons line in their reply but shipped artifacts without one, and the policy blocked the merge both times. The reply is transient; the artifact survives.

instruction: Delete rhetorical lines and clauses a newer rule supersedes when you consolidate a charter.
outcome: The 'never assert from memory' clause was removed once agreement 11 covered it. PO intake steps were compressed from 3 to 2, and a duplicate rule was deleted.

instruction: As your last action, write your status row: COMPLETE, AWAITING ASSIGNMENT, with a one-line verdict and the artifact path, or BLOCKED naming the blocker. Write it to a per-agent row file, never to a shared dashboard file in the main checkout; the coordinator merges rows with a script.
outcome: Several agents editing the shared dashboard deadlocked both merge trains on 2026-09-08. The Architect charter body (:74-77) still says to update the shared dashboard, while its card says per-agent rows, an unresolved inconsistency.

instruction: Work autonomously end to end without pausing for approval, which is standing. Do full diligence first: RED-first TDD, both test roots, all gates, and a multi-device battery for sync, money or schema changes. Stop only for destructive or owner-gated operations (data deletions, purges, fleet deploys) or genuine scope decisions.
outcome: Owner directive of record (working agreement #1).

instruction: Send every design fork, blocking finding or disagreement between agents to an LLM judge along with the source evidence. The ruling binds. Adversarial panels review before risky merges.
outcome: Owner directive of record (working agreement #2).
enforcement: none (charter text); decide workflow per CLAUDE.md

instruction: Keep owner interruptions to a minimum: batch questions to the owner into one list, prefer test paths that need no login, and write one-paragraph certifications, never play-by-play.
outcome: Owner directive of record (working agreement #5).

instruction: On any breakage, impact-analyse the most recent diff and its blast radius BEFORE suspecting the environment or a pre-existing defect.
outcome: Owner directive of record (working agreement #7).

instruction: Leave nothing unowned. Every defect, residual or stale file you find goes to the product owner as a fix or removal requirement before the in-flight work merges.
outcome: POLICY 9f rejects unowned residuals.

instruction: End every artifact FILE (not your reply) with a 'Lessons:' line that names only the lesson ids whose triggers fired, in the form 'Lessons: L-3: clause, L-8: clause' with no commas inside a clause; 'Lessons: none' is valid. A REJECTED verdict names a 'New lesson: L-N', which lands before re-certification.
outcome: POLICY 9c rejects an artifact without the line and reads the file, not the reply. POLICY 9d requires the new lesson to land before re-certification.

instruction: A judge reviews every stage's artifact AND its execution: what was grounded versus assumed, what reachable thing was missed, whether the handoff carried what the next stage needs. Each capability finding becomes a durable upgrade to that role's charter (a new check, a sharper procedure, a named trap), logged under '## Charter upgrades'. Repeating a gap already found is a process defect, escalated.
outcome: Produced the dated '## Charter upgrades' lists in both charters: about 20 Architect entries and about 60 Developer entries, each tied to a judge finding. POLICY 9k blocks a REWORK that has no dated charter upgrade.

instruction: A judge who did not write the code reviews every implementation against the spec, AC by AC, and for correctness, before the work is called done. The verdict, APPROVE or REWORK, is committed as '<ID>-judge-review.md'. Self-review does not count. REWORK re-enters at the spec. One post-delivery judge on the same tree is enough; never run a third.
outcome: Green TDD is not done: the Developer stops and hands nothing off until APPROVE. Not running duplicate judges saves tokens.

instruction: A stage that produced no artifact has not completed, however good its prose report. Never start without your predecessor's artifact: no plan without the spec, no code without the plan.
outcome: Makes every stage boundary checkable by whether a file exists.

instruction: Where the generic constitution and the project instructions file disagree, the project instructions win and the constitution is the defect. Say so; do not follow the constitution.
outcome: Settles which source wins.

instruction: Delete charter rules as readily as you add them. When a newer, broader rule covers an older one, remove the older one and record the deletion.
outcome: Deleted: 'fail-open only where blocking would be worse' and 'an uncited constant BLOCKS the spec' (Architect), and four Developer hard rules that duplicated CLAUDE.md, plus the fourth copy of 'never report done on unit tests alone'.

instruction: Write one ledger line at hand-off, then your status row.
outcome: The board is derived from the ledger.

instruction: Run the check commands; do not recite them. Keep one canonical copy of any list, such as the merge gates, and point to it, because a second copy goes stale the day it is written.
outcome: The gate list grew from five to eight within two sessions, so copies elsewhere went stale.

instruction: Report the RED proof, green counts, gate results and what you did NOT verify. Update the TDD record and tick the boxes.
outcome: Reports stay faithful and name the unverified parts.

instruction: Send every design fork, blocking finding or inter-agent disagreement to an LLM judge with the source evidence. The ruling binds. Run adversarial panels before risky merges.
outcome: Working agreement 2. Later realised as decide.js and the judge's decision mode.

instruction: Minimise owner interruptions: batch owner asks into one list, prefer login-free test paths, and write one-paragraph certifications, never a play-by-play.
outcome: Working agreement 5. Unmeasured.

instruction: On any breakage, impact-analyse the most recent diff and its blast radius BEFORE you hypothesise environment issues or pre-existing defects.
outcome: Working agreement 7. It also cuts the other way: an already-broken flow is graded INCONCLUSIVE, not blamed on the change (test-agent.md:114).

instruction: Let nothing float unowned: every defect, residual or stale file found anywhere goes to the product owner as a fix or removal requirement before the in-flight work merges.
outcome: POLICY 9f rejects unowned residuals under '## Residuals'.

instruction: End every artifact with a 'Lessons:' line as its LAST line. Name only the lesson ids whose trigger fired, one clause each with no commas inside a clause, or write 'Lessons: none'. It goes in the file, not the reply.
outcome: POLICY 9c blocks the artifact without the line. The policy file itself records 9c being inert across a whole new artifact chain once (policy_check.sh:851).

instruction: A REJECTED verdict names 'New lesson: L-N', and that lesson lands in the ledger before re-certification.
outcome: POLICY 9d holds re-certification until the lesson lands.

instruction: Have a judge review every stage's artifact AND the agent's execution (what was grounded vs assumed, what reachable thing was missed, whether the handoff carried what the next stage needs). Apply each capability finding as a dated line under '## Charter upgrades' in that agent's charter. An agent repeating a known gap is a process defect, escalated.
outcome: Working agreement 10. Produces every Charter-upgrades line in these files. POLICY 9k blocks a REWORK without a staged charter upgrade.

instruction: After TDD and before calling work done, have a judge who did not write the code review it AC by AC and for correctness. Commit the APPROVE/REWORK verdict as '<ID>-judge-review.md'. Self-review is not this step, and REWORK re-enters at spec.
outcome: Working agreement 12. Unmeasured.

instruction: Write the verdict file with per-criterion results, suite and gate numbers, device evidence and residuals, ending CERTIFIED or REJECTED (each reason routed to the owner of its fix). Only CERTIFIED releases the next requirement.
outcome: Defines the test-report artifact. Unmeasured.

instruction: On REJECTED, establish provenance before asserting any mechanism: tag each cited line NEW, DORMANT-MADE-LIVE or UNTOUCHED via 'git diff main -- <file>'. An untouched line with production mileage is not the mechanism unless the diff made its path live.
outcome: Paired with the Mechanism/Suspects split (L-4).

instruction: Split a rejection's diagnosis into 'Mechanism (proven)' and 'Suspects (unproven)'. A mechanism needs a file:line per hop, must explain EVERY symptom including timing and silence, and must pass a differential (a path that works on the same build and why it is spared). Suspects become their own requirements and stay out of the mechanism.
outcome: Two hygiene suspects rode into a root-cause narrative and the amendment round shipped its own defect (L-4; history agent-test-agent.md:420-423).

instruction: Make your LAST action a closing row: 'COMPLETE, AWAITING ASSIGNMENT' with a one-line verdict and the artifact path, or 'BLOCKED' naming the blocker and stating the requirement is PARKED.
outcome: Without the row the agent sits idle and the pod loses a stage. Blocked work is parked, never staffed (history agent-test-agent.md:177-189).

instruction: Where a vendored constitution or template disagrees with the project's top-level instructions file, the instructions file wins. Report the constitution as the defect.
outcome: Precedence rule. Unmeasured.

instruction: Allow one rework round: deliver every blocking finding as a COMMITTED probe that is RED on the tip, so rework is 'make these green'. Re-certification runs only the committed probes plus the delta.
outcome: ONE REWORK ROUND (2026-09-05). Cuts re-certification to the probes plus the delta. Unmeasured.

instruction: Fix non-blocking findings forward yourself (units, figures, wording, a one-sided pin you can complete) in your own docs/test commit, listed as 'fixed forward', never sent back as rework.
outcome: Avoids extra rework rounds. Unmeasured.

instruction: Ticking a box is a claim: tick only with a quoted passing run (the command and its success line). A leg you did not run is written NOT-RUN.
outcome: BINDING [B-2].

instruction: Write one ledger line per hand-off (requirement, stage, verdict, one-line note) to an append-only ledger that the board is derived from.
outcome: REQ-138 append-only event ledger. The 53-branch triage found 44 branches blocked by a single missing ledger event (card:74-77).

instruction: Keep each authoritative list (e.g. the gate list) in exactly one place and reference it. A second copy goes stale the day it is written.
outcome: The gate list grew from five to eight inside two sessions. The cards' own 'eight gates' is already stale against the eleven in CLAUDE.md, which proves the rule.

instruction: Never decide product questions as orchestrator. Escalate only rulings (an AC no run can meet, a scope or dependency question, a design hole the probes exposed), early, one sentence each with a recommended answer. Decide and record everything else.
outcome: Operating method 12. Unmeasured.

instruction: Root-cause before a fix: name the cause in one sentence, then act. Never re-run in hope. A step that failed twice the same way is a process defect: escalate, do not retry.
outcome: Operating method 6. Unmeasured.

instruction: Resume from disk after any interruption. A killed step's files are the next step's starting point; nothing is re-derived, nothing a predecessor wrote is deleted, and you never resume from a chat channel.
outcome: Directive #32 and orchestrator BINDING [B-3].

instruction: Keep the state true in the same action: the step that did the work writes the ledger line and the context section, never 'later'. A stale record is worse than none.
outcome: Operating method 9. A resuming session trusts the state file.

instruction: Report faithfully, outcome first: what passed, what failed with its output, what was skipped and why, and what only a device can prove. Never present inferred as observed.
outcome: Operating method 11. Unmeasured.

instruction: A step blocked twice on the same cause becomes a ruling. A task you have flagged twice is a PROCESS defect and goes to the owner.
outcome: Orchestrator BINDING [B-4].

instruction: Never copy a developer's figure into the defect register. Re-derive the number from the tree, or leave the cell empty and say why.
outcome: The register is the instrument the zero-defect policy is measured with, and an unreproducible line in it is worse than a blank.

instruction: (Superseded) Compute the next decision id at write time as max+1 with a grep one-liner, never by hand.
outcome: Picking ids by hand left D41, D42 and D51 each heading two entries. The grep-at-write-time replacement still raced: two unstick judges both wrote D146 in the same minute (history agent-judge.md). Replaced by decision_add.py, which allocates under a file lock (judge.md:28,80). The orchestrator files still carry the old one-liner.

instruction: Record every ruling only through a locked allocator script (body: DECISION, WHY with the file:line you opened, and what evidence would overturn it), then add one context line under '## Judge rulings' citing the id. Never type, remember or grep a decision id.
outcome: Duplicate ids from hand-picking and from racing grep-at-write-time (D41, D42, D51 doubled; D146 written twice in one minute). decision_add.py also supports disjoint id blocks per parallel session.

instruction: Shape every judge verdict as PASS or REVISE with at most five corrections, the hallucinations found, token findings and at most five directives. Write the directives into the context file under '## Judge rulings', dated and naming the stage.
outcome: Every agent reads the ctx file first, so rulings reach them.

instruction: Never edit the artifact you judge; its producer revises it.
outcome: The judge's toolset (Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Write) carries no Edit.

instruction: Score every pass against a per-feature evaluation file: exact design values generated by a script, screenshot diffs against reference shots with calibrated bars, and the judge's own criteria. At the first pass, write up to 25 measurable criteria, each naming its check (test, script, metric or inspection) and pass bar, ordered by impact. Every verdict lists each row scored and its result.
outcome: Directive #58. Unmeasured.

instruction: Iterate until the judge is satisfied: a REVISE repeats until PASS. Never pass to be kind, and never hold work to a bar the team cannot see; add the criterion to the evaluation file first.
outcome: Directive #59. Unmeasured.

instruction: Have the judge rule every product, scope, copy, UX and trade-off question that would otherwise wait for the owner (open rulings, PO deviations, role disagreements) at the first pass that sees it. Never park it.
outcome: Owner directive #57: decide on the owner's behalf, Steve-Jobs strict.
owner_words: judge should make decisions on my behalf and move the project forward, judge should be very strict as steve jobs

instruction: List owner-only physical acts (credentials, OAuth clients and consent screens, billing, console clicks, deploys, store uploads) once, never rule them, and decide everything around them so the rest keeps moving.
outcome: Defines the owner-only boundary. Unmeasured.

instruction: Never weaken a safety rule to move faster: fail-closed registration and activation, backward compatibility, frozen production identifiers, security.
outcome: Hard limit on the judge's authority. Unmeasured.

instruction: End every verdict with the next concrete step, so the team never waits on a question.
outcome: 'Move it forward' (history agent-judge.md).

instruction: For owner-wait decisions (merge go, product stance, scope, trade-off, process change), the judge verifies the load-bearing facts itself (checks on the named head, open review threads, the code) and returns GO, NO-GO or the chosen option with every condition, recorded and with the next step. One-way decisions get a product view and a technical view first, and the judge rules where they disagree. The GO satisfies the merge gate's explicit-go item.
outcome: Directives #51 and #63. Unmeasured.
owner_words: judge the situation as the best po and technical expert in world and give his go.

instruction: Call a judge the MOMENT a lane stalls (a step ends with work left, the verifier gets no result, or the same blocking findings return after a fix), not only at gates. Within 15 calls it names the CAUSE from evidence (lane summaries, ctx log, job logs, other lanes' and requirements' ctx) and tests the common causes: an unlanded dependency, an unowned file, a dead or refused job, a spec gap, a loop on one finding.
outcome: REQ-306's stuck run on 2026-10-07 had 48 agents, 18 of them idle, and 0 judge calls (history agent-judge.md).
owner_words: help in case anyone is stuck.

instruction: Target each unstick correction at a lane key (it goes to a fix step) or at the orchestrator (in your order), and record any ownership or scope ruling in the decision log.
outcome: Unstick protocol steps 2 and 3. Unmeasured.

instruction: Never answer an unstick with 'wait', which is the scheduler's job. PASS only if the lane is not stuck.
outcome: Waiting belongs to jobs_wait.sh.

instruction: Never give a correction that starts, collects or re-checks a test job, battery or gate run. The verifier runs right after the corrections land.
outcome: 2026-10-07: unstick corrections sent fix steps to launch and collect batteries, and they looped on 'no result yet', the same waste the scheduler had just removed (history agent-judge.md).

instruction: Treat 'close enough' as REVISE: any difference from the approved design (layout, copy, motion, spacing, colour, timing), a stub, TODO, placeholder, mocked production path, skipped or deleted test, swallowed error, dead end, missing failure/offline/resume state, missing theme or orientation, or an unneeded tap. End to end means the real flow from first tap to live, with every failure recoverable in plain words. Defer only a named owner-only action.
outcome: Owner: very strict, no corners cut. Unmeasured.

instruction: Run the mechanical pre-judge checkers (citation rot, task DAG, coverage matrix, citation pins, invariants, affected tests) before every judge, and have the producer fix their failures first. The judge cites the report, never re-opens what it covers, and spends its calls on what no script can see.
outcome: Measured on REQ-306: 14 h, 23 REVISEs in 30 verdicts. Six of seven wave-2 REVISEs named no product defect, and spec plus design took 13 serial rounds. prejudge.sh on that tree found the drifted pins, the missing coverage matrix and the rotted citations in 2 min 20 s.

instruction: Check direction: every part traces to the owner's words, the oracle or a recorded decision. Scope creep, gold-plating, re-litigating settled decisions, or a longer, wordier or less forgiving customer path are corrections.
outcome: Judge check 1. Unmeasured.

instruction: Check truth: verify the three riskiest claims yourself (open the file:line, run the cheapest refuting command, check the named test or file exists). No evidence, a citation not saying what is claimed, or an unreproducible count is a hallucination, and REVISE if it concerns code, tests or product. An agent miscounting its own calls or tokens is only a token finding.
outcome: Judge check 2. Unmeasured.

instruction: Check product honesty: no animation or sentence claims progress the system has not made, and no copy promises what research shows is untrue for this customer.
outcome: Judge check 3. Unmeasured.

instruction: At the design gate, check for duplicated code on this branch AND every unmerged branch with the overlap script, and rule each row that shares new names or code paths.
outcome: A cross-branch audit (50 agents, ~6.3M tokens) found a requirement re-deriving fixes two open PRs already held, while branch_overlap.py existed (it runs in seconds) and nothing referenced it (history agent-judge.md).

instruction: Check repo law and name the rule applied: module boundaries, additive-only backward compatibility, frozen production identifiers, cited constants, RED-first tests, every test root.
outcome: Judge check 4. Unmeasured.

instruction: Check user-friendliness: fewest taps, plain words, a way out of every failure, readable contrast and sizes, reduced motion, and tablet ergonomics in both orientations.
outcome: Judge check 5. Unmeasured.

instruction: Check traceability: every changed file and test maps to a task node, every node to the plan, every plan item to a spec AC. Work with no node is out of scope: REVISE to remove it, or have the PO add the node.
outcome: Directive #64. The mechanical half is prejudge's task-dag and coverage-matrix checks.

instruction: Check security: cite this tree's security, tenant-isolation and tenant-rules gate results. Access-rules changes need their rules test run. No credential, token or code in a file or log, and every tenant read and write scoped to its tenant. A security finding is always a product defect; take the safer fix.
outcome: Directive #64. Unmeasured.

instruction: Check performance: cite the performance gate and the evaluation file's read, write, cold-start and latency budgets. Nothing blocks the UI thread and no spinner lacks an end. A measured regression is a product defect.
outcome: Directive #64. Unmeasured.

instruction: Check guardrails: every listed gate and the policy check ran green on this tree, and no guard was weakened, skipped or bypassed without a recorded reason in the override log. A bypass with no reason is a REVISE.
outcome: Directive #64. Overrides are logged to .claude/scratch/guard/denials.jsonl.

instruction: Write each correction in one or two sentences naming the file, the change and the reason. Vague coaching is not a correction.
outcome: Unmeasured.

instruction: Reserve REVISE for PRODUCT defects (correctness bug, unmet AC or evaluation row, hallucination about code, tests or product, broken repo rule, dishonest screen, departure from the owner's words). Process findings (call caps, token waste, report wording, an uncertified pass on right code) become directives and charter upgrades, never a round. PASS with directives is normal.
outcome: REQ-306: 23 REVISEs in 30 verdicts, six of seven wave-2 REVISEs with no product defect, 14 h of run time (history agent-judge.md). Directive #61.

instruction: On the first spec or design round, run three parallel lens judges (correctness, owner, testability). Each reports every finding under its lens and writes no ruling; the next single judge merges them into one set of rulings.
outcome: Directive #61. Unmeasured.

instruction: Make every statement in a verdict carry its evidence; the judge is held to the same rule as the team.
outcome: Unmeasured.

instruction: Before prescribing a tool or mechanism to a role, read that role's tools list and name only tools it holds. If a tool is missing, ask the orchestrator to grant it and state what is sanctioned meanwhile.
outcome: REQ-305 spec-r3: rulings told the PO to Edit, but the PO's charter grants no Edit. Two folds were scored as failures for the whole-file Read/Write their toolset forced.

instruction: Before naming the values, readers or read sites a branch, stored id or guard depends on, grep the producers and every use, open each helper and state its miss branch. Name only what can actually reach it.
outcome: D38: must-not-fire rows built on values that never reach the branch would pass vacuously. D111 missed an agent-side reader. D113 counted one read site and wrote 'accept' when a second site forwarded misses, so the spec gained a row RED for the wrong reason.

instruction: Before citing a mutation row as anchoring a code line, grep its find-string in the product code and name the enclosing function.
outcome: D49 cited a row whose find text matched only a line in a different function, so the prescribed check could not fail on an edit to either guarded line. The citation reached the design, the ctx and a dispatch title.

instruction: Before calling a count a hallucination, make the refuting grep match what the claim counts: a file set by its import path, a symbol by its declaring file. Open one extra hit before ruling.
outcome: D51 'refuted' a correct count of six users because a bare class-name grep also matched four tests importing a second class of the same name.

instruction: Before an artifact passes, run once, exactly as written, every local read-only proving command it names, and reconcile its text about WHEN things happen (commits, wave starts) with the recorded rulings.
outcome: D56 passed a plan whose named check exited with Errno 2 on bare names, and whose commit timing contradicted an earlier ruling.

instruction: Before setting a pixel or visual bar, open the ONE reference shot most likely to break it and list what it shows that the product will not draw.
outcome: D69 demanded EXACT matches against shots carrying a demo cursor and a sketched sheet that the design hides on purpose (D70).

instruction: Before scoring, verify every edit an earlier ruling owes this pass, with one grep per edit scoped to its node lines (not the whole file) and in literal spelling. A proof that an expression is GONE excludes lines naming it as forbidden or as a mutant.
outcome: D80/D81 never checked an owed edit, so certify launched on a stale form. D136's whole-file grep would have made a fold delete a correct node. D118 demanded an expression count of 0 AND a mutation row restoring it, an unreachable bar.

instruction: Before binding a write's scope key (tenant, owner, device) to a value, grep the writer that stores it and the reader that returns it. Take scope keys from the session, never from the row being scoped.
outcome: D118: a ruling bound a pull's claim to the row's own tenant field, which comes from an unscoped read, leaving one realistic cross-tenant row.

instruction: A criterion that greps a tree-wide diff must say how it attributes lines in a shared tree. Before scoring a tester's failure count as a lane defect, compare the tested file blobs with the log's timestamps.
outcome: REQ-322: one criterion read another requirement's files as this one's, so it could fail only on parallel work. A tester's 19 failures came from another lane's mid-rework timer that was gone at the next blob.

instruction: Before prescribing a test table over a switch, print its arms and cross only the members whose arm reads the crossed input. Results returned outside the switch get their own rows.
outcome: D111/D112: an 'every member x every status' table expected outcomes the code never returns (the status is read in one arm of three) and dropped an interactive declined result.

instruction: Before a design or its lane table passes or is REVISEd, run a set difference of spec ACs minus design ACs (comm -23) once.
outcome: D123: four ACs, including a blocking one, stayed unrouted through a full round.

instruction: Before prescribing a new RED row, guard or test file, or deleting catalogue entries, grep the existing tests for the constant, URL or catalogue it pins AND for the file path, then extend the existing file.
outcome: D132: tasks planned two new test files while an existing test already pinned the same constant (an unowned break). A contract test read the catalogue by path, which an id-name scan never finds.

instruction: Before prescribing a rules or test assertion for a path, grep the decision log for that path or collection and carry every recorded clause (id lists, member function, nesting) into the prescription.
outcome: D135: a prescribed RED row could not fail on a dropped id list the decision log had already decided.

instruction: At orientation, find and rule every question routed to the judge this pass with one broad grep covering the explicit, arrow, passive ('parked on/owed by the judge') and 'decide' forms.
outcome: D141: a routed question sat through eight passes and 493 tool calls because each judge scored only its own lanes. D146: arrow and passive forms were missed for ten steps and eight no-op continuations. D155: decide forms were missed too.

instruction: Before an unstick rules a lane 'waiting' or 'queued', ls the stuck nodes' files, check they are tasked, read the lane's last tester VERDICT lines, and read the remaining nodes by role. Another role's items left there ARE the stall.
outcome: D146: a design ruled ten screen files 'built now'; none existed and none was tasked. D149 ruled a lane 'QUEUED, not looping' while its tester had REJECTED it.

instruction: An unstick that has corrections is REVISE even when the lane's code is right, because a PASS routes nothing.
outcome: D161: unstick() returns null on PASS and routes corrections only on REVISE (judged-swarm.js:309).

instruction: Before prescribing a scrubber or redactor as a keyword guard, run it on the keyword with a name that contains it as a substring. A guard should strip only the exact echoed value.
outcome: D190 -> D218 era. A substring guard would mangle ordinary names.

instruction: Before calling a code path 'shipped' in a REVISE, grep its callers and follow one up to a UI screen or widget handler. A method with no such caller is not the shipped path.
outcome: D216 named an authentication method that has no UI caller, which cost a rework round.

instruction: Use the judge at every stage gate and after every build wave, and have it watch every agent and artifact, not just final output.
outcome: Owner instruction 2026-10-06 (#56).

instruction: Back every process rule with numbers measured on this repo; the measurement is the argument for the rule.
outcome: The skill exists because a 20-line fix had been wrapped in twelve ceremonies and a 3,182-test suite run sixteen times; every figure in it was measured 2026-09-14/15.

instruction: A derived status board must count every completion path, including work absorbed into another branch.
outcome: defect_board.py derived MERGED from retirement tags, and absorbed cards had none. MERGED went 105 -> 114 after the fix; the board had told the PO more work remained than did.

instruction: When you find a broken instrument: reproduce it (paste the command and output), fix it, then prove the fix RED to GREEN with a control in which an absent literal still FAILS.
outcome: Without the control, a 'fix' may just make everything pass.

instruction: Report an instrument fix as a before-to-after figure (e.g. 'BLOCKED 20 -> 0').
outcome: The skill holds that these sentences stop the class recurring.

instruction: Tier review by risk. Money/sync/schema MUST items get two independent reviews (certifier and judge in parallel); everything else gets one certifying-judge pass.
outcome: Owner directive #33, a throughput directive.
owner_words: smart strategy, not tokens

instruction: Skip a failure class only with a stated reason, and report the classes you skipped.
outcome: Makes uncovered classes visible to the reviewers.

instruction: In the same action as a launch, record the run id, script path and journal path in the state file and the memory pointer.
outcome: Lets a resuming session find the run.

instruction: On a spend-limit or API kill, read the run journal first, then resume from the run id. Cached steps return instantly; null steps re-run from the files on disk.
outcome: Nothing a killed agent wrote is lost (#32).

instruction: Make the PO a step in the run. A planning step returns questions; a PO step rules from the card, directives, domain and lessons, amends defective ACs and re-plans, for at most two rounds.
outcome: Introduced 2026-09-08 so rulings no longer wait for the human session.

instruction: Escalate to the human only decisions reserved to them: money semantics, production data deletion, credentials/accounts, the live customer account, fleet deploys, the release go, relaxing a directive. Decide everything else.
outcome: Keeps the owner out of routine rulings.
enforcement: PO step returns owner_questions only for the reserved list

instruction: Nothing merges on a red gate, and the PO never overrides a gate.
outcome: No measurement given.
enforcement: train verdict BLOCKED with red output

instruction: Retry an agent step that died on an API error up to 3 times, telling it its files are on disk: continue, never start over.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: Report 'not_verified': what only a real device or environment can prove.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: Reviewers fix forward non-blocking findings (units, figures, wording, a one-sided pin) and list them. Blocking findings travel as committed RED probes.
outcome: Owner directive #33: one rework round instead of churn.

instruction: A REWORK verdict names the role at fault and a concrete charter rule.
outcome: Feeds charter upgrades (POLICY 9k per CLAUDE.md).

instruction: An independent judge outside the delivering team, in its own detached tree, attacks the invariant the card protects with the schedule that breaks it (two clients, offline, reorder, clock skew, restart). It checks merge-tree against main and backward compatibility, files each blocking finding as a committed RED probe, and commits its review.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: Allow exactly ONE rework round on the committed probes, then re-certify. A re-certification that does not pass goes to a ruling, not another loop.
outcome: Later CLAUDE.md #59 says iterate until the judge is satisfied.

instruction: If a MUST item reaches the train without a judge verdict, run the judge first. A blocking judge finding after rework goes to a ruling.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: Return a structured verdict: summary of 25 lines or fewer, each finding with file:line, the blocking subset listed, not_verified stated.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: Run product delivery as a staged team (product owner -> analyst -> architect -> developer -> tester), each stage a spawned agent with a charter. The main session only orchestrates.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: Settle inter-agent disagreements and design forks with a one-shot judge given both positions and the source evidence. Its ruling binds; user-gated calls go to the user.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: Run an adversarial review panel before risky merges.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: The repo's CLAUDE.md always outranks pipeline convenience.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: Report, never ask: at backlog approval, for each certified requirement (one paragraph), for each merge and tag after the fact, and for anything owner-gated.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: Fix and merge autonomously end to end. Stop only for destructive or owner-gated operations and genuine scope decisions.
outcome: Working agreement #1.

instruction: Minimise owner interruptions: batch owner asks into one list, prefer login-free test paths, keep certifications to one paragraph.
outcome: Working agreement #5.

instruction: On any breakage, analyse the most recent diff and its blast radius BEFORE suspecting the environment or pre-existing defects.
outcome: Working agreement #7.

instruction: Nothing floats unowned. Every defect, residual or stale file found goes to the product owner as a fix/removal requirement before in-flight work merges.
outcome: Working agreement #8.

instruction: Paste the current lessons file (rules tier at least) into every stage spawn prompt. The charter's read-it-yourself instruction is only the fallback.
outcome: Judge-panel amendment 2026-08-27. The lessons file is not auto-loaded.

instruction: End every stage report with a 'Lessons:' line and a 'Domain:' line naming only the rule ids whose trigger fired. A REJECTED verdict names its 'New lesson: L-N', which lands before re-certification.
outcome: No measurement given.
enforcement: POLICY 9c (Lessons line), POLICY 9d (new lesson before re-cert)

instruction: Judge every stage on both the artifact and how it was executed. Apply each capability finding as a dated entry under '## Charter upgrades' in that role's charter; a repeated gap is a process defect.
outcome: Working agreement #10: each iteration starts stronger than the last.
enforcement: POLICY 9k blocks a REWORK without a charter upgrade (per CLAUDE.md)

instruction: A judge who did not write the code reviews every implementation AC by AC and for correctness, committing APPROVE or REWORK as <ID>-judge-review.md. REWORK re-enters at spec. One existing post-delivery judge on the same tree is enough; never run a third.
outcome: Working agreement #12.

instruction: Land a lesson or domain rule earned by one team before any other team's next stage spawn.
outcome: So the second team never repeats the first team's mistake.

instruction: Send dependency contention to a judge early: is the edge real, can the item split, which order carries less risk. Record the ruling beside the edge so it is never re-argued.
outcome: 'An idle pod costs a cycle, a judge round costs minutes.'

instruction: Reviewers and judges must come from outside the team that delivered.
outcome: Every blocking defect caught before a device (a tender-gate zero, a tautological recurrence guard, an unmeetable AC, two unpinned production call sites) was found by a reviewer with no stake.

instruction: Every item's artifacts name the team that serviced it. A branch reaching merge with no team named is a process defect.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: Update the state file at every dispatch, merge and blocker. A stale state file is worse than none, because a resuming session trusts it.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: Judges re-run delivered evidence on ONE detached tree at the delivered sha plus ONE trial merge into main, and cite the committed merge-tree table. A conflicting trial merge is reported and the judge stops: no compositions, sibling gates, custom conflict resolvers or ratchet regeneration.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: Judges refute with rows (a patch against the committed battery, run once, stated as uncommitted). Never ad-hoc scripts, scratch copies in a tree, or edits to source. An unrelated flake gets one verdict line.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: Every orchestrator turn, and at least every 15 minutes while agents run, run a health watch (idle minutes, last tool call, interrupted/denied/timed-out results) that exits 1 on STUCK or INTERRUPTED.
outcome: Owner directive #29.
owner_words: we must make arrangement to resolve interruption when someone is stuck, po are you not keeping a watch on your agents, you must keep an eye on your agents and help when there is a resource deadlock or interruption.

instruction: For a hung tool, find the agent's child process, kill only that process, and relaunch the agent from its partial files if it did not recover.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: For a permission denial, the orchestrator judges whether the step is legitimate, performs it itself if so, and relaunches the agent with the result pasted. A --no-verify with a stated reason is the orchestrator's call, never an agent's.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: For a harness block (refused sleep, Bash timeout), put the avoiding idiom in the dispatch prompt (background run, bounded loop, output to a file). A second sighting is a prompt defect owned by the orchestrator.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: For a resource deadlock, serialise: one agent per worktree, suites in separate detached trees, locks released by name.
outcome: Two suites in one tree clobbered each other's SQLite fixtures (REQ-110 R-3).

instruction: After a spend-limit kill, relaunch every killed agent from disk in one turn, never one at a time.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: When the orchestrator stops an agent on purpose, say so in the state file in the same action, so the owner never sees an unexplained kill.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: Record every stuck or interrupted event (agent, cause, remedy, minutes lost). A cause that recurs twice becomes a rule.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: Trains with no app-code diff (scripts/tests/docs) carry a standing go-ahead (review + judge verdict + train gate). Trains with app code need the go once per train.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: Paste the domain-rules file into every stage spawn alongside the lessons file. The product owner gets the whole file at intake and curation.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: Memory is an index, never a rulebook. Any binding rule found mid-session lands in the lessons file or CLAUDE.md in the same commit as the work that earned it; a rule found only in memory counts as unwritten.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: Edit duplicated working agreements only in the canonical block, then run the sync script.
outcome: A policy check blocks any commit where the six copies diverge.

instruction: Each requirement's activity-log entry carries an 'Orchestration:' line: verification rungs climbed (with smoke checksum), every re-dispatch and why, and any orchestrator lesson.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: Delete charter rules that merely restate another rule or contradict one.
outcome: 2026-08-27: removed a standing-autonomy section, a 'keep the user in the loop at merges' bullet and a merge-cadence trailer. All restated agreements #1/#5, and the merge clause contradicted #1.

instruction: Keep replies to 100 words or fewer; a review lists findings, never narrative.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: Report the order actually followed. If it diverged from the printed order, say so; never back-fill a DAG to match what you did.
outcome: No measurement given.

instruction: Mark local changes to vendored tooling with a banner, and keep a script that asserts each change survives an upstream regeneration. Run it after every upgrade.
outcome: 'specify init' overwrites the skills wholesale and would silently delete four owner directives. 'A rule nothing checks gets forgotten; this repo has proven that five times in one session.'

instruction: Have every agent read the binding rulings (the decisions log) first, using grep -n and bounded windows, and obey them.
outcome: Rulings made earlier bind later steps. Without this, steps re-litigated or contradicted decisions already made.

instruction: Before any agent and again before any judge, run a mechanical evidence guard on the task node. Stop the run if the node was closed by a ruling (CLOSED-BY) or the clean tree already has a GREEN evidence line. A missing answer fails closed.
outcome: Earned in REQ-406 O2 round 14 (F4/F10): judges kept being dispatched on a node a ruling had already closed.
enforcement: scripts/pipeline/evidence_guard.sh (rc 0 allow, 2 usage, 3 CLOSED-BY, 4 already GREEN), wired at outcome-first.js:29-37

instruction: Log a one-line audit tally: working path steps out of total, code gaps, and owner-only steps.
outcome: Gives an at-a-glance progress observable for the outcome.

instruction: When a gap needs a product ruling before code, do the parts that need none, keep the gap open, and return the question in a structured 'ruling' field: facts with file:line, the options, and reversibility (two-way unless it changes a document shape, a schema or a shared project). Never wait for the ruling and never guess it. The orchestrator gets it ruled inline by the decision workflow.
outcome: Earned by REQ-323 (2026-10-07): three fix steps were spent blocked on two product rulings and nobody asked the decision judge.
enforcement: DEV/STEP schema 'ruling' + workflow('decide', ...) call at outcome-first.js:67

instruction: A fix step that finished nothing, or changed only bookkeeping files (scratch/ctx notes, activity log), while the open-gap list did not shrink, made no progress: stop the fix loop. Cap fix iterations at 6.
outcome: Earned by REQ-323: the old no-progress test never fired because each blocked step changed bookkeeping files.

instruction: REVERTED rule: do not count any changed file as progress. A no-progress test that accepts bookkeeping-only edits never fires.
outcome: The old test failed: 16 continuations 'progressed' on a ctx line alone, costing 29M tokens. It was replaced by the bookkeeping-excluded progress test.

instruction: Report test counts from the LATEST run of each command only. A run superseded after you fixed your own test goes in the summary, never in the results list.
outcome: Stale red runs no longer trigger false REVISEs, and stale green runs no longer mask failures.
enforcement: prompt text; red computed at outcome-first.js:86-87

instruction: The proof's 'left' holds ONLY product failures on the outcome path, each with file:line. Notes, follow-ups and anything a host test cannot cover go in the summary, because anything in 'left' stops the judge.
outcome: Stops follow-up notes from blocking the judge.

instruction: Decide a blocked path by rule, not by a judge agent. If any gap is left open, there is no proof, the proof has work left, or a proof test is failing, return REVISE (judged:false) and spend no judge.
outcome: Earned by Bugbot on PR #35: a judge agent was spent where a rule could decide. Rule-decided verdicts are scripts (#50).

instruction: Have the outcome judge judge ONLY the outcome: does the path work end to end, safely? It reads the git diff of exactly the files the steps changed, plus the proof report. It returns REVISE only for a product defect on the path, naming where and the smallest fix, and PASS when the path works end to end on the fakes and is safe.
outcome: One judge per outcome instead of a judge per stage.
enforcement: Judge phase prompt + VERDICT schema; cap 15

instruction: At every judge gate, check the security and performance guardrails: data isolation between customers/tenants, fail-closed provisioning and behaviour, no credentials in files or logs, no UI-thread blocking, and backward compatibility (no stored-document shape change, additive-only schema migrations).
outcome: Implements the judge charter checks 7-10 (#64).

instruction: Check traceability at the judge: every change must trace to an audited path gap (outcome mode) or to a task node (backlog mode), and every ticked box must have its test.
outcome: Untraceable changes are caught as waste or scope creep (#64).

instruction: Show the judge the list of deferred process items and have it REVISE if any of them is really a product gap on the path, naming it.
outcome: Stops workers from hiding product gaps in the deferred list.

instruction: Record every judge verdict and ruling in the decisions log ONLY through the atomic id-allocating script (it takes the next D-id under a file lock, above every id on fetched remotes, and prints it). Never pick the next id by reading the file.
outcome: Duplicate ids happened five times (D41, D42, D51, D132, D146 on 2026-10-07, when two unstick judges ruled in the same minute). Two machines also both wrote D165.
enforcement: scripts/pipeline/decision_add.py (fcntl lock + git fetch/grep over remotes)

instruction: Give the judge the persona of the greatest system designer in the world, and have it follow its committed charter's checks exactly.
outcome: Implements owner directive #64.

instruction: Whenever a decision would otherwise go to the owner (a merge go, a product stance, a scope call, a trade-off, a process change), invoke the decision judge instead. The PO writes the facts, the judge rules and records it, and the PO acts in the same turn.
outcome: Directive #51 said this on 2026-09-29, but its charter lived in an uncommitted scratch file and was lost. The merge gate still asked the owner, so the PO kept asking. decide.js is the committed mechanism.
owner_words: Llm as judge should be invoked whenever my decision is need, llm should judge the situation as the best po and technical expert in world and give his go.

instruction: Commit every process mechanism (charter, workflow, rule) to the repo. A rule living only in an uncommitted scratch file will be lost.
outcome: Directive #51's charter was lost from scratch, so the PO kept asking the owner for decisions.

instruction: Encode the protocol as code (a workflow script), not prose. A rule written only as prose is followed until someone forgets it.
outcome: This is why the swarm order, gates and brakes live in judged-swarm.js.

instruction: Scale review to reversibility. A two-way (reversible) decision gets one ruling judge. A one-way decision first gets two parallel lens views (product and technical), then a ruling judge who settles any disagreement and says why.
outcome: Keeps cheap decisions cheap and gives irreversible ones two independent views.

instruction: Never rule on owner-only physical acts (credentials, OAuth clients and consent screens, billing, console clicks, deploys, store uploads). The judge names them for the owner and decides everything around them.
outcome: Separates what only a human can physically do from what the judge may decide.

instruction: Refuse a decision request that lacks a question and facts.
outcome: Returns an error before any agent is spent.

instruction: The decision judge verifies every load-bearing fact itself before relying on it (open the file, run the cheapest command, read the check runs), within at most 15 tool calls, and never reads a large file whole.
outcome: Stops rulings from resting on unverified claims supplied by the requester.

instruction: The decision judge rules on the owner's behalf, as the best product owner and best technical expert would, strict and with no corner cut. It never hands the question back.
outcome: Stops the judge from bouncing decisions back to the owner.

instruction: A lens agent gives ONE view only and writes no file. Only the ruling judge records.
outcome: Keeps one writer for the decisions log.

instruction: Define the two decision lenses. Product: the customer, the owner's words and objective, scope, user experience, what ships. Technical: correctness, money and sync safety, backward compatibility with older clients on the same data, security, and the evidence behind every claim.
outcome: Gives one-way decisions two independent views covering complementary risks.

instruction: Every ruling body states the DECISION, WHY (naming what was opened) and what would overturn it. The ruling returns GO / NO-GO / CHOSEN, every condition the GO depends on (for a merge: CI green on the named head and no open blocking review thread), the owner-only acts and the next concrete step.
outcome: Makes rulings actionable and reversible on stated evidence.

instruction: Never report done for a check you did not see pass.
outcome: Honest reporting.

instruction: After the build, judge the requirement WHOLE: against its spec, every acceptance criterion, the task file's AC-coverage sections and the evaluation file. Read the diff stat against the base, then open what each AC needs. Run any doubted test, and return REVISE only for a product defect with file:line and the smallest fix.
outcome: One whole-requirement judge after the build, capped at 25 calls.

instruction: After a REVISE, a Developer fixes ONLY the judge's defects, each RED first, then runs dependency tests. Judge again, up to maxRounds (default 3).
outcome: Judge, then fix until PASS, bounded.

instruction: Every swarm gate loops produce, judge, revise until the judge PASSes. A gate still at REVISE after maxRounds (default 4) STOPS the run and returns its state with the reasons. A REVISE never passes a gate.
outcome: Implements #59: a stop with reasons is better than a run that pretends.
enforcement: judged-swarm.js gate() and stage early returns (:267,:276,:285,:294)

instruction: State the product objective, the requirement brief, the approved design (the oracle the product must match exactly) and the evaluation file the judge scores against in every swarm agent's prompt. The evaluation metrics are every agent's metrics.
outcome: Every agent optimizes toward the same objective and scoring.

instruction: Run the repo's mechanical checkers (a prejudge script) before every judge. The producer fixes their failures first (up to 2 times), and the judge reads and cites the prejudge report, never re-checking what it covers.
outcome: Measured on REQ-306: 14 h, 81 agents, 23 of 30 judge verdicts REVISE. Six of seven wave-2 REVISEs named no product defect, and four of six wave-3 REWORKs were failure classes the repo already had scripts for.
owner_words: i will go by your proposal make the rule to save tokens
enforcement: scripts/pipeline/prejudge.sh (rc 0 clean, 1 FAIL, 2 refusal; report .claude/scratch/prejudge/<REQ>-<stage>.txt); clearMech() in judged-swarm.js:153-162

instruction: A REVISE names a PRODUCT defect: a correctness bug, an unmet spec AC or evaluation row, a false claim about code, tests or product, or a breach of the owner's words. Process findings (call caps, token waste, miscounted reports, wording) go in tokenFindings and a charter upgrade, and never make a REVISE by themselves.
outcome: Six of seven REQ-306 wave-2 REVISEs were process-only. Each cost a whole round.

instruction: A lens judge reports EVERY finding under its lens in one pass, not just the first few, and writes no shared file. The next single judge records the merged rulings.
outcome: Fewer rounds, and a single writer for ctx and the decisions log.

instruction: A single (non-lens) judge writes its directives into the ctx file under ## Judge rulings, dated and naming the stage, and records product decisions in the decisions log.
outcome: Rulings are durable and the next stage greps them.

instruction: The judge follows its charter exactly within at most 15 tool calls, scores against the evaluation file listing each row, and returns: scored rows, corrections (target/change/why), hallucinations to remove, token findings, new directives, owner-only items, and the next step.
outcome: Gives structured, routable judge output.

instruction: Judge corrections are binding: the producer applies each one, says how, and removes every flagged hallucination.
outcome: The revise loop is driven by explicit corrections.

instruction: Define progress strictly. A continuation progressed only if its remainder got shorter, or it changed a non-bookkeeping file without lengthening the remainder. A node 'done' that changed and shortened nothing is not progress, and a step with nothing done, changed or left is empty-handed, not finished. On no progress, stop and send the remainder to verification as unfinished.
outcome: Sixteen continuations 'progressed' on a ctx line alone, costing 29M tokens.

instruction: A step whose continuations run out with work left is STUCK. Flag it, and the caller calls the judge at once.
outcome: Feeds the unstick mechanism (#56).

instruction: Merge a run's step deliveries into one: lists accumulate (deduplicated for files and not-run items), texts join, and the caller decides the remainder.
outcome: One coherent delivery report across continuations.

instruction: Relaunch failed jobs at most twice. A relaunch starts only what the collect named and never redoes a probe or row that already exists.
outcome: Keeps relaunch loops bounded.

instruction: End every spec, plan and task file with a 'Lessons:' line naming only lessons whose trigger fired, one clause each, or 'Lessons: none'. A pre-commit policy check refuses the commit without it.
outcome: Implements agreement #9.

instruction: A fix pass fixes each item at its root with a RED-first test, re-runs the lane tests, analyzer and affected gates, and never widens scope.
outcome: Narrow, proven fixes.

instruction: Never drop a judge correction. Corrections addressed to the orchestrator, or to work no lane owns, are applied by one developer step in the judge's order, honouring every 'after (n) lands' and editing only files some lane owns.
outcome: REQ-306 stopped on 2026-10-06 when all five of D141's corrections went to 'orchestrator' and none matched a lane key.

instruction: Call the judge the moment a lane stalls: a step ends with work left, its verifier gets no result, or the same blocking findings return after a fix. The judge finds the cause (cross-lane or cross-requirement dependency, unowned file, environment fault, spec gap, loop on one finding), gives targeted corrections, records any ownership or scope ruling, and PASSes only if the lane is not actually stuck. Allow at most 2 unsticks per lane.
outcome: REQ-306's stuck run had 48 agents, 18 of them idle, and 0 judge calls, because judges ran only at stage and wave gates and a stuck lane never reached its gate.
owner_words: i asked llm as judge to review all tasks and help in case anyone is stuck

instruction: REVERTED rule: do not run the judge only at stage and wave gates.
outcome: With gate-only judges, REQ-306's stuck run had 48 agents, 18 idle and 0 judge calls. Replaced by unstick-on-stall.

instruction: Detect loops by fingerprinting the blocking findings. If the same set comes back after a fix, escalate to the judge instead of fixing again.
outcome: Breaks fix loops on a single finding.

instruction: Gate each wave: clear the prejudge build checks by routing fixes to their lanes (up to 2 times), then judge the wave on its owned-file diffs, tests, ctx Log and transcripts (for token waste) against the spec, design and evaluation file. Correction targets must be lane keys.
outcome: Each wave must pass before the next starts. NOT SATISFIED stops the run (:399).

instruction: When a run stops, return its full state: which stage stopped, the outputs so far, judge verdicts and side tracks. Never return a pretended success.
outcome: Resumable runs and honest reporting.

instruction: Appoint an LLM judge that rules in the owner's place on one stated product objective (best finished product, fewest tokens, shortest duration consistent with it). The judge is read-only except for the decisions file it writes.
outcome: Every later ruling (D1 to D1231) was made by this judge, or recorded by the PO as an owner ruling, so the owner was not asked for any non-physical decision.
owner_words: invoke LLM as a judge who wants to build the best self-guided, self-managed POS product, for any decision you need from me

instruction: Every ruling names what it rests on: the file:line the judge opened, or 'queue fact' for a fact the requester supplied and the judge did not re-derive.
outcome: Rulings carry 'WHY (opened this pass)' blocks. Evidence can be re-checked later instead of re-argued.

instruction: Write every decision in a fixed shape: DECISION, WHY (evidence opened), RISK and bound, REVERSIBLE?, OVERTURNED BY (the evidence that would reverse it), WHO ACTS (owner-only acts named separately).
outcome: A later session can revisit a ruling when its overturn condition fires instead of re-arguing it. Many rulings cite an earlier OVERTURN clause as 'not fired' (e.g. D738/D739).

instruction: When ruling on a request packet, record a 'queue corrections' list: every fact in the request that was false, imprecise or missing, measured on the tree.
outcome: Caught a CLAUDE.md size claim (~1,200 lines vs a measured 1,469 lines / 95,156 bytes), a missing writer for reservations, and a store build that shipped a refusal 'TODAY'.

instruction: Treat an instruction-file trim as an audit: a rule a script enforces costs nothing to shorten. Any rule that is neither on the card nor behind a script gets one or the other, or is deleted.
outcome: Overturn condition: a REWORK within two weeks traced to a dropped, unenforced rule restores that rule only.

instruction: A rule that names a tool which does not exist gets routed around. Either drop the rule or deliver the tool, and until then do not cite it in dispatches.
outcome: CLAUDE.md named run_flows.sh and test/flows, and neither existed. D54(3) later made the cited runner real instead of adding a new one.

instruction: No agent writes its own tool-call count into a context file. The judge measures counts from transcripts.
outcome: Third miscount in a row (r2, r4, r5): the ctx log said 11 calls and the transcript had 12. A count written before a step ends cannot include the calls after it.

instruction: Compute decision ids by script at write time (max + 1, within a per-worktree id block). Never hand-pick an id.
outcome: D41, D42 and D51 each headed two entries. decision_add.py raises when a worktree's block is full, and a full block once stopped a ruling from being recorded (D750).

instruction: Before a ruling names a code path, reader or seam, grep for it. When a ruling's own error is found, record 'judge defect, owned' with a dated charter upgrade in the judge's charter.
outcome: Defects inherited from the judge's text into specs: a 'draft decode' named without a grep, a read-site count of one that became 'refused', and a verifier the judge named but never checked.
enforcement: .claude/agents/judge.md '## Charter upgrades' (POLICY 9k blocks a REWORK without one)

instruction: After a container or machine restart, treat every background job as dead. No log written before the restart counts as evidence.
outcome: Every background job died in the 2026-10-07 container restart.

instruction: Cap unstick rounds per lane (two). After the cap, the next verifier pass that finds only test-rig findings APPROVES the lane and records the rig items as the test agent's.
outcome: A lane spent 3 hours in verify/fix loops on three harness items, none product. Each round cost ~30-60 min of the only machine and ~20M tokens.

instruction: When a lane stalls on failures, classify each one as harness or product. Fix harness defects only in the harness, and never change product logic to make a golden or fixture pass.
outcome: 21 golden rows failed on a rig that never reached its scene: a harness defect. A real dispose-callback crash was found alongside and fixed RED-first.

instruction: A tool that records MERGED, DELIVERED or GREEN must measure the fact against the remote base. Fix the whole class of such tools when one is found assuming.
outcome: wave.sh recorded MERGED after a local merge. branch_health.sh measured nothing in a clone without a local main and still said GREEN. Both were fixed, and ~40 more diff-scope reads were carded.
enforcement: complete_branch.sh BASE=origin/main; close_all.sh refuses without fetch

instruction: A test build's delivery note names every gate RUN with its evidence and every gate NOT RUN, plus what the user will now see.
outcome: The note listed RUN (branch health, judge suite, battery 18/18, analyzer, diff coverage) and NOT RUN (local CI on the composed tree, full suite, device leg).

instruction: The implementer never grades its own work. The orchestrator spawns independent judges (e.g. one visual, one functional), each grading every criterion and citing the logs it opened. Any REVISE goes back through a developer fix step and the same judges on the new sha.
outcome: The Developer was dispatched twice for a grading role its charter forbids, and stalled. That was a routing defect, not a Developer defect.

instruction: When judges return structured output, the orchestrator transcribes it verbatim into the grade file in one COMMIT step, adding, removing and re-scoring nothing.
outcome: Workflows spawn judges for schema'd output, so the returned output is the judge's artifact of record. This ended the stall on writing the grade file.

instruction: When a run keeps dispatching against a fixed script, suspect a stale run loaded before the edit: stop it and relaunch from disk. A third ruling on the same point goes to the orchestrator as a process defect, not to another ruling.
outcome: Round-18 dispatches came from a run that loaded the old script. This was the fourth ruling on the same point.

instruction: Record load conditions in the evidence row next to any timing verdict. Timings taken under high load are inadmissible as baselines, and a met verdict is not re-measured.
outcome: 20 of 21 arm launches ran above load 3.0. The verdict stood with the caveat, and no timing key was recorded.

instruction: Never overwrite an evidence log. Freeze each run under its tree stamp and name the next run anew. The runner refuses to start when its log already exists.
outcome: An r2 evidence log was overwritten by a re-run, which made a ruling's citation stale.
enforcement: r2 script exits 3 when its suite log exists

instruction: State plainly in a ruling what was NOT verified (e.g. a liveness check the sandbox refused, or an output the judge did not observe).
outcome: 'Liveness of the runners themselves was NOT verified (ps is refused by the sandbox)'. 'this output was NOT observed by the judge'.

instruction: Keep goalposts fixed: no reference or expectation is moved toward the app without a recorded ruling. Show this by diffing the references.
outcome: The preview was unchanged since its approval commit, and reference changes came only through ruled patches.

instruction: Criteria a judge marked 'not scored' are not part of the bar. Do not hold a grade for them. File valid enhancements as the NEXT outcome instead of polishing while the outcome is ungraded.
outcome: F3/F4 phone polish was filed to backlog. Green r2 evidence was kept rather than thrown away by a re-anchor and r3 run.

instruction: Enforce rules at the tool call, not in prose: install a PreToolUse hook that refuses forbidden habits and states the sanctioned route.
outcome: Over 294 swarm agents every rule was already written in CLAUDE.md and still violated: 43 agents waited on their own jobs in sleep loops, developers ran a median 11 min against a 3-min rule. 'Writing them down had already failed.' The guard fired live in this session (refused a 221-line sed window).

enforcement: scripts/pipeline/tool_guard.py wired as PreToolUse (Bash|Read) in .claude/settings.json; tests scripts/pipeline/test_tool_guard.sh

instruction: Give every guard a logged escape hatch with a stated reason (# guard-ok: <reason>), log every refusal and override to a JSONL file so the guard's value is measured, and fail open on guard bugs.
outcome: Measured, not asserted (directive #47); a guard bug must never strand a session.

instruction: Run the repo's existing mechanical checkers (citation rot, task DAG, coverage matrix, citation pins, invariants, affected tests) before any judge; the producer fixes failures first; save the report with the tree sha so the judge cites it.
outcome: One swarm: 14 h, 81 agents, 23 of 30 judge verdicts REVISE; 6 of 7 wave-2 REVISEs named no product defect and 4 of 6 wave-3 REWORKs were classes the repo already had scripts for.
owner_words: can we find innovative ways to finish fast with 10 times better quality

instruction: Print, at every session start, a brief computed from the repo naming the specific open opportunities and recently-violated rules; prose read once gets competed with.
outcome: Two three-day-old directives were violated, ~830k tokens spent hand-driving the rig while automation sat one step away.

instruction: Assert by script that every owner directive still has its live enforcement text in the file that carries it.
outcome: The prose register rots; refactors and charter rewrites could silently drop a directive ('a rule nothing checks gets forgotten').

instruction: Keep an append-only event ledger (merge=union in .gitattributes) as the single writer of stage transitions; boards and dashboards are projections of it.
outcome: Transitions were hand-recorded in three places and drift kept winning: the board read REWORK for two merge-ready cards.

instruction: Derive status boards from repository evidence, never hand-edit: stage by artifact precedence, columns summing to the card count, MERGED verified in git (tag or merge commit), disagreements shown, and a --check that fails on a stale committed board.
outcome: Retirement tags are never pushed (fresh clones under-report) and fix docs were not merge signals for two merged cards; a stale board is trusted by a resuming session.
owner_words: update the defect board after each fix and update the latest status

instruction: Share one implementation of report-verdict parsing between the ledger and the board; a backfill refuses to write twice and a merge adds only missing events.
outcome: Two parsers could disagree about what a report said; a double backfill would count every historical event twice.

instruction: Validate dashboards against git and lock state, and exit non-zero when a dashboard contradicts reality.
outcome: A stale dashboard is worse than none because assignments are made from it (L-11).

instruction: Allocate decision-record ids atomically under a lock, above every id on fetched remote branches, and inside a per-session disjoint id block.
outcome: Duplicate ids happened five times locally plus a cross-session collision when two parallel sessions both took the same id.

instruction: Attribute a red batch gate by computation: intersect the failing test files with the tests that reach each card's changed files; exonerate and re-drain unreached cards; a failing test no card reaches is main's own defect.
outcome: A drain reverted three good cards for one bad one; hand attribution cost two suite runs and ~40 min. The method found a pre-existing app-version break on main.

instruction: Generated reports must not use LLM-assigned or stale labels; derive labels by a stated mechanical rule and print the coverage share behind each.
outcome: The report described a 7,283-node graph while graph.json held 12,802; 48 communities carried conflicting stale names.

instruction: Re-pin file:line citations shifted by a merge mechanically; refuse when the token no longer exists.
outcome: Re-pinning was paid by hand three times and blocked a 12-branch train a fourth time.

instruction: Check that local modifications to vendored skills/templates survive a tool upgrade that overwrites them.
outcome: A routine 'specify init' would silently delete four owner directives living inside vendored skill files.

instruction: Never commit sentences describing volatile external state (e.g. CI status); query it live, distinguishing jobs that never started from jobs that failed.
outcome: Every committed CI-state sentence was true when written and false within days; budget refusals and real failures both read 'completed failure'.

instruction: Deliver a test build only through one script: build the named commit in its own worktree, verify signer fingerprint and app id, and write a delivery note naming what was verified and what was not; never claim a gate it did not run.
outcome: Deliverables reached the owner untested ('should work').
owner_words: i need 100 times better quality with delieverables

instruction: Compile one evidence file for the judge generated from disk facts (criteria, verdicts, traceability, rulings, open findings, self-check).
outcome: About half of 49 judge findings were missing-evidence or process findings.

instruction: Measure throughput from a signal only success can create (retirement tags), never estimate; a target without a meter is a slogan.
outcome: Two earlier 'N warnings' claims were false because nobody re-measured; merge commits over-count and boards under-count.
owner_words: keep running and ensure every hour we fix at least 15 cards

instruction: Install the same defaults (account-wide rules, the tool guard, the hook settings) into every repo's sessions through the environment setup script, from one embedded source, stepping aside where a project ships its own guard.
outcome: Repo files bind only one repo and ~/.claude does not survive cloud sessions.

instruction: Publish shared tooling from a single source by assembling copies only in the output; never commit a duplicate copy inside the source repo.
outcome: Keeps the public toolkit and the host repo from drifting.

instruction: Close every assignment by setting your status row to COMPLETE (verdict + artifact path) or BLOCKED naming the blocker with the item PARKED, so the coordinator reassigns immediately.
outcome: Without the row an agent sits idle and the pod loses a stage; later moved from the shared dashboard to per-agent row files.

instruction: Update the state file and dashboards in the same action as each dispatch, merge or blocker.
outcome: A resuming session trusts a stale state file.

instruction: Read the mechanical prejudge report first and cite it; spend judge calls only on what no script can see.
outcome: Judges had spent rounds on citation and count errors scripts already catch.

instruction: Judge direction: every part of an artifact traces to the owner's words, the oracle or a recorded decision; scope creep, gold-plating and re-litigating settled decisions are corrections.
outcome: Judge check 1.

instruction: Judge truth: pick the three most load-bearing claims by risk and verify each yourself; an unverifiable claim about code, tests or product is a hallucination and makes the verdict REVISE.
outcome: Judge check 2; agents miscounting their own tokens is a token finding, not a REVISE.

instruction: Judge product honesty: no animation or sentence may claim progress the system has not made.
outcome: Judge check 3.

instruction: Judge user-friendliness: fewest taps, plain words, a way out of every failure, readable contrast and sizes, reduced-motion support, ergonomics in all orientations.
outcome: Judge check 5.

instruction: Limit a judge to 15 tool calls per pass; REVISE only for product defects; process findings become directives and charter upgrades and never cost a round by themselves.
outcome: Directive #61: rounds were burned on process findings.

instruction: On the first spec/design round run three parallel lens judges (correctness, owner, testability) that report findings only; the next single judge records merged rulings.
outcome: Directive #61.

instruction: The judge decides on the owner's behalf at first sight of a question, records each ruling via the atomic id allocator with WHY (file:line) and what would overturn it, and ends each verdict with the next concrete step; only owner-only physical acts wait, and no safety rule is weakened for speed.
outcome: Work waited on the owner for decisions.

instruction: Call the judge the moment a lane stalls (unstick mode): name the cause from evidence, give corrections that unblock now, never answer 'wait', and never prescribe starting or re-checking test jobs.
outcome: A stuck run had 48 agents, 18 idle, 0 judge calls; unstick corrections that launched/collected batteries looped on 'no result yet'.

instruction: Score every stage against a per-feature evaluation file open to the whole team: generated exact values from the approved reference, calibrated screenshot bars, and judge-written measurable criteria each naming its check and pass bar; a row with no cited output at a tree sha is UNSCORED, never met.
outcome: The team iterates until the judge passes it.
